description: PROC REG ordinary least squares -> statsmodels OLS, with intercept, OUTEST=, OUTPUT predicted/residual, and listwise deletion.

proc_reg_ols.title: PROC REG MODEL y=x1 x2; -> sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit(); intercept by default unless NOINT.
rule: `MODEL y = x1 x2;` -> `sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit()`. SAS includes an intercept by default; add one with `sm.add_constant` unless `NOINT` is specified.
`OUTEST=` writes one row of parameter estimates; reproduce parameter names + estimates for QC.
SAS drops rows with any missing model variable (listwise deletion) -> `df.dropna(subset=model_vars)` before fitting.
pitfalls: Forgetting sm.add_constant drops the intercept and shifts every coefficient.
Not applying listwise deletion changes n and every estimate versus SAS.

code: res = sm.OLS(d[y], sm.add_constant(d[X])).fit()     # intercept unless NOINT
